query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

cited_evidence.text: The CrMnFeCoNi high entropy alloy particles reinforced NiAl composites were prepared by MA and SPS process. The microstructure, mechanical, and tribological properties of the composites were investigated. Based on the test and analysis, the following conclusions can be drawn: 1. The distribution of HEA phase is relatively uniform after SPS. Under the high temperature SPS process, elemental diffusion occurs between the matrix phase and the HEA reinforcement phase. The addition of HEA will decrease the grain size of the composites and generate some Al2O3 particles at the grain boundary. 2. The density and hardness of the composites increase with the increasing of HEA content. Both the ultimate compressive strength and yield strength increase remarkably with an increasing weight fraction of the HEA. The YS and UTS of composites increase from 779 MPa to 1566 MPa and from 2121 MPa to 2692 MPa, respectively, which should be attributed to the second phase hardening effect and fine grain strengthening effect. 3. The addition of HEA will slightly increase the COFs of composites and accelerate the abrasive wear, and the reason can be attributed to the reduction of oxide film on the surface o

Addition of ceramic reinforcements to the fcc matrix HEA have also been tried for the development of high entropy composites that can exhibit better combination of strength and ductility. High entropy composites have been developed by vacuum arc melting, mechanical alloying,,, spark plasma sintering,,, vacuum hot pressing, hot iso-static pressing, and additive manufacturing, processes. Carbides, oxides and nitrides such as WC, Al2O3, SiC, TiC,, TiN and Y2O3 have been used as ceramic reinforcement for the development of HEA composites. Selection of a suitable HEA matrix and ceramic phase is particularly important to design and develop strong and tough HEA composites. In the present work CoCrFeNi has been selected as the matrix material. Varying amounts of SiC have been added to CoCrFeNi HEA and their effect on the microstructure, phase structure and mechanical properties have been investigated.
